text: RUSI reports that in 2023 each Russian axis commander kept an orbit of Orlan-10s over the fighting and the artillery brigade flew its own Orlan-10 complex, so Ukrainian troops were often watched by two separate Orlan groups, each able to call different fires.

RUSI estimated the time from Russian drone detection to rounds on target at about 3–5 minutes with an organic drone, against about 20–30 minutes when the target came from EW detection or went through a fire-control headquarters.

Russian Lancet strike videos counted by the Russian LostArmour site, as reported by Forbes, rose from about 25 a month in early 2023 to a peak of 135 in July 2023 and 126 in August 2023, then fell to 50–90 a month.
RUSI says Lancet-3Ms "scoured" the narrow Ukrainian breaches in the 2023 counteroffensive and hunted Ukrainian artillery so persistently that Ukrainian guns could not be brought forward.
An Atlantic Council analysis saw "no tactical advantage besides occasional Lancet drone strikes" on the Russian side at Vuhledar in February 2023.

notes: The research file adds that no source found documents Russian FPVs at Vuhledar in February 2023.

cites.quote: often heralded by the lifting of GPS jamming

text: RUSI reported that Russian electronic protection dipped whenever Russian units needed precise coordinates.
The Orlan-10 reconnaissance drone has a ceiling of 5,000 m, a reported specification given "according to open sources" by Armada.
The Orlan-10's reported endurance is up to 16 h (UNN, 2026) or up to 18 h (Ukrainska Pravda, 2022); the sources disagree.
The Orlan-10's reported speed is up to 150 km/h, with a range of 90–150 km/h.
The Orlan-10's reported reach is up to 120 km on its link and up to 600 km "offline" or with a relay.

text: Ukrainian military sources reported in 2017 in Donbas that the Orlan-10 reconnaissance drone works at 1–1.5 km altitude and the relay drone at 4.5–5 km or higher.
An Orlan-10 group usually has two or three aircraft: reconnaissance, EW and relay.
According to Armada, an Orlan-10 "master" aircraft talks to the pilot on a 930 MHz link and relays commands to two "servant" aircraft carrying an optronic and a COMINT payload.
UNN reports that the Orlan-10 carries Full HD zoom cameras, infrared and thermal imagers, radio direction finders and EW equipment.
The Orlan-30 laser-designates for Krasnopol guided shells, and more Orlan-30 flights were observed in spring 2023, according to Ukrainian interviews given to RUSI.
According to Armada, Orlan-10s form part of the Leer-3 EW system, one system per brigade, which detects and jams cellphone traffic and can inject fake text messages.
RUSI notes that Leer-3 is hard to synchronise with other EW.
The Supercam S350 is a Russian reconnaissance drone for mapping and monitoring terrain and targets.
Two Russian Supercam S350 drones were shot down over Mykolaiv Oblast on 20 March 2023.
Lancet targets are found by Orlan-10 or SuperCam drones.
RUSI singled out the Orlan-10 in 2022 as a cheap platform with "high performance" that "proved difficult to counter".
RUSI judged that the Orlan-10's inertial navigation "makes insufficient account of windage".
RUSI judged that the Orlan-10 flew at medium altitude and was "too cheap to be economical targets for air defences".

cites.quote: too cheap to be economical targets for air defences

text: According to RUSI, Russia "did not have enough of these platforms to sustain the loss rate" of Orlan-10s in the 2022 Donbas battle.

cites.quote: did not have enough of these platforms to sustain the loss rate

text: RUSI estimated from Ukrainian interviews that in 2022 a Russian unit with its own UAV took 3–5 minutes from detection to effect.
RUSI estimated that in 2022 a Russian fire request via a fire-control headquarters took 20–30 minutes at tactical level and about 48 hours at operational level.
RUSI estimated that detection to effect for Russian Orlan-10 complexes in spring 2023 "remains rapid at around 3–5 minutes".
RUSI estimated that a Russian engagement cued by EW detection took about 20–30 minutes in spring 2023.
Armada states that a three-ship Orlan-10 flight took within 10 minutes from identification to rounds (2022).
A Ukrainian unit spokesman reported that in 2022 Russian AeroScope detection of a DJI operator led to the start of targeting in "as little as five or six minutes".

cites.quote: as little as five or six minutes

observations.value_text: as little as five or six minutes
observations.subject: AeroScope detection of a DJI operator to start of targeting

text: In June 2023 Ukrainian M777 crews displaced 2–15 minutes after opening fire, depending on their distance from Russian threat systems.

RUSI's 20–30 minute fire-loop figure appears twice: for a request routed through a headquarters (2022) and for fires cued by EW detection rather than a drone (2023); these measure different chains and both are interview-based estimates.
Armada's "within ten minutes" figure for the Orlan-10 fire loop sits between RUSI's 3–5 and 20–30 minute figures and is not sourced to fieldwork.

RUSI describes three interlocking Russian "reconnaissance fires circuits" in 2023: a direct link from a drone team to its guns, a link through fire control to a battery, and a higher headquarters assigning alternative "means of destruction" against a detected target.
According to RUSI, the Strelets system let Russian specialist infantry (VDV, Wagner) pass sensor detections straight to the guns, so the commander "is on, but does not need to be in the loop".

cites.quote: is on, but does not need to be in the loop

text: In one December 2022 Russian assault, four drones worked at once: one on Ukrainian artillery, one on reserve routes, one ahead of the assault group and one over the assault group itself (RUSI).

observations.subject: drones working at once over one assault

text: In summer 2023 Russia "doubled down" on its reconnaissance-fires complex, prioritising Krasnopol production and increasing drone designation for it (RUSI).
A Ukrainian explainer says the Orlan-10 is "quite difficult to spot, both visually and on radar" and "quite difficult to shoot down".

cites.quote: quite difficult to spot, both visually and on radar

text: Ukrainian units downed Orlan-10s with MANPADS; on 1 May 2022 alone Ukrainian forces reported neutralising 10.
The Ukrainian answer to the Orlan-10 in 2023 was "a combination of countermeasures involving electronic warfare stations and firepower".

cites.quote: a combination of countermeasures involving electronic warfare stations and firepower

text: Ukraine's Bukovel-AD EW system has been in service against the Orlan-10 since 2016.
Armada argued that the Orlan-10 master aircraft's 930 MHz link could be passively detected and jammed, and that killing one aircraft takes the whole three-ship group out.
In late 2023 a Ukrainian EW station was announced with the stated aim to "blind Zala and Orlan so that they can no longer adjust their Lancets to our positions".

cites.quote: blind Zala and Orlan so that they can no longer adjust their Lancets to our positions

text: Radar-cued interceptor drones began thinning Russian Orlans and Zalas only from late 2024 (RUSI).
RUSI's spring-2023 description of Russian Orlan orbits at axis and artillery-brigade level comes from interviews covering December 2022 to May 2023, the window of the Vuhledar assaults.
notes: The research file adds that no fetched source documents a specific Orlan or Zala at Vuhledar.

text: Russian commentators described the Russian tanks attacking Vuhledar in early 2023 as "blind, deaf" columns without situational awareness.
At the start of the 2023 counteroffensive, Ukrainian troops had to train for "up to 25 UAVs observing their movements" (RUSI).

cites.quote: up to 25 UAVs observing their movements

observations.subject: Russian UAVs observing a Ukrainian unit's movements

text: In the 7 June 2023 attempt south of Mala Tokmachka, the second Ukrainian group was spotted by Russian drones and hit by artillery.
In October 2023 a 65th Mechanised Brigade sergeant near Robotyne said Russian artillery guided by reconnaissance drones was the main problem, more than Russian counterattacks.
The Lancet comes as the Lancet-1 with a warhead of about 1 kg and the Lancet-3 with a warhead of about 3 kg.
RUSI says the Lancet-3M improved warhead effect and economy of design.
Reuters, relayed by RFE/RL, reported in July 2023 that the newest Lancet models carry a warhead of "up to 5 kg", which conflicts with the 3 kg reported elsewhere.
RFE/RL reported in July 2023 that the Lancet has a radius of ">40 km".
Kyiv Post gives the Lancet's range as 40–70 km.
In autumn 2023 Lancets struck about 65 km from Russian-held ground, a demonstrated case.
The Lancet's reported endurance is about 40 minutes.
A Ukrainian adviser gave the Lancet's cruise speed as about 100 km/h (July 2023).
Kyiv Post gives the Lancet's cruise speed as 80–110 km/h and its speed in the terminal dive as about 300 km/h.
The Kyiv Independent gives the Lancet a "stated top speed of around 300 km/h".

cites.quote: stated top speed of around 300 km/h

notes: The file notes that the speed figures measure different flight phases.

text: The Lancet-3 weighs about 12 kg and the Lancet-1 about 5 kg.
Oryx estimated the cost of a Lancet at about $35,000 (relayed by RFE/RL).
Kyiv Post estimates the Lancet's cost at $30,000–35,000.
The Lancet is catapult-launched and sends video from its nose camera.
The Orlan-10 can carry a radio repeater to extend the Lancet's control range.
The Lancet's developers claim a mode in which it flies to a preloaded area and scans for targets without an operator link.
The Lancet was unveiled in 2019 and used in Syria, and was "not seen until July 2022" in Ukraine (Forbes).
Oryx-logged Lancet use rose from about October 2022.
Kyiv Post dates Russian use of the Lancet to autumn 2022.
At Vuhledar in February 2023 an Atlantic Council analysis saw "no tactical advantage besides occasional Lancet drone strikes" on the Russian side.

cites.quote: no tactical advantage besides occasional Lancet drone strikes

text: The monthly Lancet strike counts for 2023 compiled by LostArmour and relayed by Forbes are videos only, and Forbes calls them "likely ... a fraction of the total".

cites.quote: likely ... a fraction of the total

text: LostArmour counted about 25 a month Russian Lancet strike videos in January–February 2023, as relayed by Forbes.
LostArmour counted almost 50 a month Russian Lancet strike videos in March–April 2023, as relayed by Forbes.
LostArmour counted 135 Russian Lancet strike videos in July 2023, the 2023 peak, with, as relayed by Forbes.
LostArmour counted 126 Russian Lancet strike videos in August 2023, as relayed by Forbes.
LostArmour counted in the 50s a month Russian Lancet strike videos in September–October 2023, as relayed by Forbes.
LostArmour counted 89 Russian Lancet strike videos in November 2023, as relayed by Forbes.
LostArmour counted 59 Russian Lancet strike videos in December 2023, as relayed by Forbes.
Forbes links the post-August 2023 drop in Lancet strike videos to a 9 August 2023 explosion at the Zagorsk optical plant, citing a Ukrainian OSINT group and analyst.
Forbes itself says "there is no proven connection" between the Zagorsk optical plant and ZALA.
A Ukrainian artillery crewman told Reuters in July 2023: "Earlier, in spring, they were not using Lancets as often as they are now."

cites.quote: Earlier, in spring, they were not using Lancets as often as they are now

text: UK Defence Intelligence called the Lancet in November 2023 "a step change" in how Russia uses small drones, increasingly prominent in counter-battery fire.
Until March 2023, Oryx's visually confirmed Lancet/Kub hits were mostly on artillery, radars and SAM launchers.
Russian counter-battery fire shifted in spring 2023 from saturating detected positions to firing Lancets, which also hunted Ukrainian guns as reconnaissance (RUSI).
In the 2023 Ukrainian offensive, Russian Lancets and FPVs "flown in complexes with ISR UAVs" struck the lead elements of Ukrainian units (RUSI).

cites.quote: flown in complexes with ISR UAVs

text: Kofman and Lee called Russian Ka-52, FPV and Lancet-3 strikes "a pernicious problem" in the 2023 counteroffensive, because advancing Ukrainian forces lacked the air-defence and EW cover they had in the defence.

Because the Ukrainian axis was narrow and "the persistent threat from Lancet-3Ms hunting Ukrainian artillery" was constant, Ukrainian guns "could not be brought forwards", so more Russian artillery could cover the lines of advance out of Ukrainian counter-battery range (RUSI).
Some videos appear to show Lancets "finishing off" vehicles already abandoned or disabled by something else (2023).
After 8 June 2023 a Lancet-3 targeted an abandoned Leopard 2A6 left from the breach south of Mala Tokmachka, with an ambiguous result.
Pro-Russian videos relayed by Reuters claimed a Lancet hit on a French CAESAR in June 2023.
One CAESAR reportedly overturned in June 2023 while swerving to avoid a Lancet.
In July 2023 a Russian Telegram video showed a Lancet striking a Leopard 2 in Zaporizhzhia Oblast; the outcome was not confirmed.
On 15 August 2023 a Lancet hit a Stryker of the 82nd Air Assault Brigade east of Robotyne, according to a Russian video; the damage is unclear.
Analyses of the 8 June 2023 Ukrainian losses south of Mala Tokmachka blame mines, artillery, ATGMs and Ka-52s, and no fetched source confirms a Lancet kill on a Bradley at Mala Tokmachka or Robotyne.
Oryx visually confirmed 113 Kub/Lancet hits and 41 misses up to early March 2023.
One Ukrainian source, relayed by Forbes, estimated the Lancet's success rate at "approximately 30%".
RUSI interviews gave the Lancet a "limited success rate", but its speed and accuracy make sustained Ukrainian firing hard (spring 2023).
A Ukrainian defence-ministry adviser claimed in July 2023 that "at least one or two" Lancets were shot down a day.

observations.value_text: "at least one or two" a day
observations.subject: Lancets shot down
observations.note: one or two a day, at least

text: The Kyiv Independent reported in November 2023 that successful Ukrainian interceptions of Lancets were "rare".
The Ukrainian Air Force counted 10,604 Lancets destroyed from February 2022 to August 2026.
Oryx's early tally of Kub/Lancet hits and misses implies that about 73% of filmed Lancets hit something.
The Ukrainian "about 30%" Lancet success rate counts all launches, including failures and shoot-downs that are never filmed, unlike Oryx's tally of filmed strikes.
A Lancet "hit" is not a kill: a net-triggered warhead "is unlikely to cause significant damage compared to a direct hit".

cites.quote: is unlikely to cause significant damage compared to a direct hit

text: Ukrainian crews put wire netting around howitzers in 2023, and both sides used metal netting around guns and equipment against Lancets.
Camouflage netting on a metal frame was rated the most effective defence against the Lancet.
Several net layers protect against the Lancet-1, but the Lancet-3 is harder to stop because its warhead can be set off remotely after it hits the net.
In one case two Lancets failed against a T-72 because a camouflage net stopped them.

observations.subject: Lancets stopped by a camouflage net

text: By November 2023 a newer Lancet pre-detonated its shaped charge to defeat nets and cages.
RUSI recommended in September 2023: "The protection of guns from Lancet-3M and other loitering munitions is also becoming a critical priority."

cites.quote: The protection of guns from Lancet-3M and other loitering munitions is also becoming a critical priority

text: The knowledge base dates Russian RF FPVs to the Bakhmut period (December 2022 – May 2023).
The knowledge base dates mass Russian use of FPVs to the Avdiivka period from October 2023.
A Russian state defence enterprise announced in May 2023 that it planned to make up to 3,000 FPVs a month (reported by Reuters).
No fetched source documents Russian FPVs or drone drops at Vuhledar in February 2023; the only Russian drone weapon an Atlantic Council analysis noted there was the occasional Lancet.
In the June–August 2023 counteroffensive Russia used FPVs together with Lancets against the lead elements of Ukrainian assaults (RUSI).
Kofman and Lee list "improvised commercial first-person-view" drones among the Russian strike assets in the 2023 counteroffensive.
When Ukrainian units had to resupply by day through narrow minefield breaches in 2023, Russian troops attacked the resupply routes "using FPV loitering munitions" and tank-fired ATGMs (RUSI).
A 47th Mechanised Brigade soldier said in September 2023 that "Russia has the edge in FPV drones", using them on vehicles, artillery and dugouts.

cites.quote: Russia has the edge in FPV drones

text: A 65th Mechanised Brigade sergeant near Robotyne said in October 2023 that Russia was increasingly using FPVs against Ukrainian equipment.
A 65th Mechanised Brigade sergeant near Robotyne reported in October 2023 a reusable Russian FPV that drops its charge and returns.
A 65th Mechanised Brigade sergeant said in October 2023 that both sides near Robotyne flew Mavic "wedding drones" to reconnoitre and adjust artillery.
In November 2023 a Ukrainian platoon commander near Bakhmut estimated Russian FPV numbers in his sector at "about double" Ukraine's, a snapshot Reuters says is hard to verify.

observations.subject: FPVs in one sector
observations.note: Ukraine : Russia about 1:2 (Russia has about double)

text: A Western analyst told Reuters that 2023 "was critical to the Russian efforts to field this tech in large numbers", referring to FPVs.

cites.quote: was critical to the Russian efforts to field this tech in large numbers

text: Russian FPVs used the 850–930 MHz band through 2023 to May 2024.

Russian FPVs were present in small numbers in spring 2023, were part of the anti-armour kill chain in June–August 2023, and were seen as outnumbering Ukraine's in some sectors by September–November 2023.
RUSI estimated in spring 2023 that Russia had about one major EW system per 10 km of front, usually about 7 km behind the front line and "usually aimed at controlling and defeating UAVs".

cites.quote: usually aimed at controlling and defeating UAVs

observations.value_text: about one per 10 km of front

text: Russian EW crews in spring 2023 were "weapons free" with "minimal interest" in deconflicting their effects (RUSI).

Russian counter-UAS kit was being pushed down to platoon level in spring 2023, "directional jammers and arrays for hijacking UAVs", with at least one system per platoon in Russian line infantry by Ukrainian assessment (RUSI).

cites.quote: directional jammers and arrays for hijacking UAVs

observations.value_text: at least one system per platoon
observations.subject: counter-UAS systems per Russian line-infantry platoon

text: Russia made "extensive use of navigational interference in the battle area" in spring 2023, which contributed to Ukrainian drone losses of about 10,000 a month (RUSI).

cites.quote: extensive use of navigational interference in the battle area

text: Eight Russian Mi-17s with EW suites were believed to operate over southern Ukraine in spring 2023, attacking Ukrainian command and control from altitude to greater depth than ground systems (RUSI).

In summer 2023 Russia moved away from large single EW platforms because Ukraine targeted emitters: Zhitel was used "much more subtly", antennas were mounted on light vehicles or dismounted, and Pole-21 was treated as "disposable" wide-area cover against drone strikes (RUSI).

Russian units reset their frequencies every 24 hours, deconflicted UAV orbits and synchronised EW with manoeuvre, so that "electronic protection would dip" when precise coordinates were needed and then come back up (RUSI).

The truck-mounted Shipovnik-Aero takes over drones, has a "sophisticated range of effects for downing UAVs", and geolocates operators for artillery; it has a low signature and can imitate other emitters.

cites.quote: sophisticated range of effects for downing UAVs

text: Shipovnik-Aero has a range of about 10 km.
Shipovnik-Aero was deployed across the front in 2023 and rated "particularly effective" by Ukrainian sources.
Pole-21 is a GNSS jammer that "creates a dome" suppressing GPS and radio-navigation-reliant equipment, built against cruise missiles, guided bombs and UAVs.
Russia claims Pole-21 has a 60 km range, while Ukrainian intelligence estimates "over 25 km".
By summer 2023 Russia treated Pole-21 as disposable wide-area cover (RUSI).
One Russian Pole-21 was destroyed in the Tavria sector, as announced on 5 November 2023.
There has been a "growing number" of reported kills of Russian Pole-21 systems since summer 2023.
The R-330Zh Zhitel jams GPS, Inmarsat, Thuraya and GSM and geolocates satcom, cell and drone control points, at up to about 30 km.
Russia used the Zhitel "more subtly" in 2023 after losses (RUSI).
The Orlan-10-borne Leer-3 detects and jams cellphone traffic and can inject fake texts; it is believed to cover 30 MHz–3 GHz, with one system per brigade.
notes: No Ukrainian or Western measured range for Leer-3 was found.

text: The Krasukha-4 targets airborne radar and UAV control links; its claimed 300 km range is unverified.
notes: The table row cites both Militarnyi sources jointly.

text: Russian Krasukha-4s were hidden under nets in forest belts in Zaporizhzhia, and one was killed near Urozhaine in November 2023.
notes: The table row cites both Militarnyi sources jointly.

text: The Russian Silok-01 / Silok-M1 detects drones, fixes their coordinates and cuts their control, telemetry and communications, with a range given as ">4 km" (Militarnyi) or 3–4 km (Jamestown).
A Silok was captured by the Ukrainian 128th Brigade in 2022, which judged it "effective only at Russian training grounds".

cites.quote: effective only at Russian training grounds

text: Russian platoon jammers and hijacking arrays provided directional jamming of drone links and drone takeover, at least one per platoon in line infantry in spring 2023; no range is stated.

Suitcase-size Russian "trench jamming stations" in trenches around Robotyne in summer–autumn 2023 cut Ukrainian drones off from their operators so that they "fall down in scores", according to a Ukrainian soldier.
The Volnorez is a Russian vehicle cone jammer that puts a "dome" over a vehicle against FPVs, from autumn 2023.
The Russian Torn-MDM intercepts and decrypts Ukrainian Motorola radios in near real time and is deployed front-wide (RUSI).
According to Jamestown, the Torn-MDM detects 1.5–3,000 MHz and locates sources up to 70 km away.
Russian EW suppressed Ukrainian radio receivers out to about 10 km beyond the front line (RUSI, spring 2023).

observations.value_text: about 10 km beyond the front line
observations.subject: suppression of Ukrainian radio receivers

text: Eight Russian Mi-17s with EW suites, giving depth from altitude, were believed to operate in southern Ukraine in spring 2023 (RUSI).
EW-equipped Russian escort helicopters with directional pods against radar flew with Ka-52 groups in the summer 2023 offensive (RUSI).
Early Russian EW focused on jamming drones' control and video links, and DJI's OcuSync "was not built for dense jamming"; a jammer that attacks both signals often leaves the drone "unrecoverable".

cites.quote: was not built for dense jamming

text: A Ukrainian operator near Bakhmut said in March 2023: "When the drone loses control, it descends and they fire at it."

cites.quote: When the drone loses control, it descends and they fire at it

text: A drone instructor on the southern front said in March 2023 that Russian EW could force Ukraine's commercial drones to land.
Shipovnik-Aero could go further than jamming and take control of a Ukrainian drone.
RUSI's 2022 data shows Ukrainian drone missions failing through jamming of the link, dazzling of sensors, or "denial of its navigational systems from determining the accurate location of a target".

cites.quote: denial of its navigational systems from determining the accurate location of a target

text: A drone that loses both its pilot link and its orientation crashes or drifts until its battery dies, and spoofing can trick a drone into thinking it is higher than it is.
Russian GNSS jamming cut the hit rate of Ukrainian Excalibur shells from 55% in January 2023 to 6% in August 2023, according to Ukrainian data relayed by Kyiv Post.
From 2022 to 2024 "the main vector of attack was the control link" of analogue FPVs (typically 900 MHz ELRS-type radios), and dedicated video jamming "first appeared in summer 2024".

cites.quote: the main vector of attack was the control link

text: Control-link jamming has favourable geometry for the defender: the drone's receiver flies towards the jammer while its transmitter stays near the operator.
In 2023 the analogue FPV video picture was mostly lost to distance and terrain, not to dedicated jammers.
In June 2023 Ukrainian converted agricultural bomber drones were "fairly binary in their viability": with Russian EW active they "could not get in and usually were not committed" (RUSI).

cites.quote: could not get in and usually were not committed

text: Russian jammers sat in layers in spring 2023: platoon jammers in the first line and the major systems about 7 km back (RUSI).
Russian suppression of Ukrainian radios reached about 10 km beyond the front line (RUSI).

observations.value_text: about 10 km beyond the front line
observations.subject: suppression of Ukrainian radios

text: RUSI found drones more useful in the defence than the attack, partly because "using them in the close against advancing troops means they are in closer proximity to their control antennae than to enemy jamming".

cites.quote: using them in the close against advancing troops means they are in closer proximity to their control antennae than to enemy jamming

text: Russian jamming ramping with depth favoured the 72nd Mechanised Brigade's quadcopters over the Vuhledar approaches and worked against the 47th Mechanised Brigade's drones flying south over the Russian belts; this is an inference from RUSI's general finding, not stated by any source for these battles.
One Ukrainian southern-front drone team lost five Mavic-3s in one week of March 2023, against two the week before.
At times in 2023 "over 2,000 Ukrainian drones have been disabled in a single week" by Russian EW.

cites.quote: over 2,000 Ukrainian drones have been disabled in a single week

notes: Euromaidan Press relays Zaluzhnyi's essay in The Economist (see 11/0055).

text: Russian EW was switched on and off, dipping for Russian precision fires and lifting for Russian aviation.
Ukrainian commanders also limited their own electronic protection to keep their drones flying, "giving freedom to enemy ISR and fires" (RUSI).

cites.quote: giving freedom to enemy ISR and fires

text: When jammed, an Asgard Group drone pilot near Bakhmut switched "to a frequency the Russians cannot easily exploit", and the picture returned within seconds (AP, September 2023).

cites.quote: to a frequency the Russians cannot easily exploit

text: The Asgard Group unit took three months of trial and error to learn to evade Russian jammers.
Ukrainian FPV video moved from 5.8 GHz towards 1.2 GHz, which penetrates obstacles better and was less jammed (reported by early 2024).
Ukrainian drone builders gained video transmitters of up to 5 W (reported by early 2024).
Ukrainian volunteer engineers made "two-way, two-signal repeaters" that "more than double the practical range" of drones (reported by early 2024).

cites.quote: more than double the practical range

text: Ukrainian volunteers patched DJI firmware and "closed the backdoors that allowed the drones to be tracked by Aeroscope".

cites.quote: closed the backdoors that allowed the drones to be tracked by Aeroscope

text: Ukrainian drone crews who pre-programmed flight paths "shielded by terrain" lived longer (RUSI, 2022).
Some Ukrainian drone crews flew without transmitting and downloaded images on recovery, at the cost of slower targeting (RUSI, 2022).
By April 2023 Ukrainian units had begun shifting to modular FPVs that were easier to adapt to Russian EW.
Ukrainian drone units hunted Russian EW antennas with the aim of a "cat-and-mouse" game (November 2023).
Mykhailo Fedorov called programming drones to strike Russian EW "on a large scale" the key task in November 2023.
In April 2022 Jamestown judged that Russian EW had "few if any recorded successes".
The Ukrainian 128th Brigade dismissed the Russian Silok EW system it captured in 2022.
By 2023 RUSI and Zaluzhnyi's essay described Russian EW as a leading Ukrainian weakness.
The difference between the 2022 dismissal of Russian EW and the 2023 view of it as a leading Ukrainian weakness is mostly time: the 2022 judgment predates the static front.

ISW reported that "multiple Russian sources" said Russian EW "severely interfered" with Ukrainian command signals, GPS devices and UAV controls during the 8 June 2023 attacks; this is a Russian claim relayed by ISW, not an observed effect.

observations.subject: Ukrainian drones downed during the Robotyne assault

text: A Ukrainian unit near Huliaipole lost three Mavics to Russian EW in two weeks in January 2023, when a Mavic had lasted six months near Donetsk a few months earlier.
Between 12 and 16 March 2022 Mykhailo Fedorov wrote to DJI that Russia used AeroScope, "an extended version ... taken from Syria", at "up to 50 km".

cites.quote: an extended version ... taken from Syria

text: DJI replied to Fedorov in March 2022 that AeroScope is built into all recent DJI drones and "cannot be turned off".
In early May 2022 Ukrainian drone operators obtained a program ("CIAJeepDoors", loaded via a USB box) that switches DJI Remote ID off without overwriting firmware.
About June 2022 DJI shipped firmware in which Remote ID can no longer be switched off, and some older models became detectable again, according to a researcher and a Ukrainian officer.
In July 2022 Aerorozvidka said "unfortunately, examples exist" of Ukrainians killed by Russian AeroScope users.
Aerorozvidka built its own R18 drones partly to evade the DJI AeroScope sensor (July 2022).
A Ukrainian drone instructor said in August–October 2022 that operator casualties were initially high because of poor security.
The Ukrainian Karlson unit said in 2022 that Russia still used AeroScope and could begin targeting a drone operator "in as little as five or six minutes", with artillery or Grad following.

observations.value_text: as little as five or six minutes
observations.subject: AeroScope detection to start of targeting

text: On 2 March 2023 Ruhr University Bochum and CISPA published that DJI's DroneID broadcasts the drone's and the pilot's location and that "the transmitted data is not encrypted"; the Mini 2, Mavic Air 2 and Mavic 3 were among the models tested.

cites.quote: the transmitted data is not encrypted

text: A southern-front drone instructor warned in March 2023 that some DJI models "can spot other drones of the same model in the area and show the original take-off position".

cites.quote: can spot other drones of the same model in the area and show the original take-off position

text: In spring 2023 Shipovnik-Aero geolocated Ukrainian drone operators "for artillery targeting".
Russian fires cued by EW detection took about 20–30 minutes in spring 2023 (RUSI).
In 2022–2023 Russian forces also struck Ukrainian UAV ground control stations directly (RUSI).
In early 2024 Ukrainian drone operators said Russia "specifically target[s]" drone operators with glide bombs and MLRS (via ISW).

mentions.name: Institute for the Study of War

text: AeroScope and DroneID gave Russia a direct position for the Ukrainian drone pilot, with a reported time to targeting of 5–6 minutes.

Direction-finding by Russian EW gave a slower operator-hunting chain of about 20–30 minutes; the 5–6 and 20–30 minute figures come from different sources and periods and are not a controlled comparison.
Ukrainian units disabled DJI Remote ID or patched it out.
Ukrainian units moved to non-DJI drones to avoid AeroScope detection.
Ukrainian drone crews practised basic site security such as hiding vehicles and sandbagging headquarters.
CNAS noted in early 2024 that Ukrainian drone operators were being hunted with drone-tracking software.
The Russian side also reflashes its own DJI drones with war firmware.
The Ukrainian defence of Vuhledar in February 2023 ran on drones: a drone feed spotted each Russian column, and shells were "adjusted by" drones or by observers on the tallest buildings.
The 72nd Mechanised Brigade flew DJI Matrice-class quadcopters and small drop drones at Vuhledar in February 2023.

The volume of Ukrainian drone footage of the 6–10 February 2023 Russian columns at Vuhledar implies that Russian EW did not deny Ukrainian ISR over the approaches; this is an inference, not a sourced statement.
The only Russian drone weapon an Atlantic Council analysis noted at Vuhledar was the "occasional" Lancet.
Russian commentators called the tanks attacking Vuhledar "blind, deaf" and without situational awareness; no fetched source names a Russian EW system at Vuhledar.
Russian EW took three Ukrainian Mavics in two weeks near Huliaipole in January 2023.
A Ukrainian southern-front drone team lost five Mavic-3s in one week in March 2023.
RUSI's front-wide picture for December 2022 – May 2023 is about one major Russian EW system per 10 km and about 10,000 Ukrainian drones lost a month.

At Vuhledar the Ukrainian side had the better drone picture, facing Russian artillery and TOS-1A fire on the town rather than a Lancet or FPV swarm; this reading rests on the absence of documented Russian drone strikes there.
The 47th Mechanised Brigade met the full Russian kill chain south of Mala Tokmachka and Robotyne in June 2023: drones spotted the columns, and artillery, ATGMs, Ka-52s, Lancets and FPVs followed.

mentions.name: drone-cued kill chain (drones spot, then artillery, ATGMs, Ka-52s, Lancets and FPVs strike)

text: Kofman and Lee wrote that in the 2023 offensive "a tank or armored vehicle will become immobilized after hitting a mine and then be destroyed by attack helicopters or drones".

cites.quote: a tank or armored vehicle will become immobilized after hitting a mine and then be destroyed by attack helicopters or drones

text: On 7 June 2023 the second Ukrainian group south of Mala Tokmachka was found by Russian drones and shelled.
Monthly Lancet strike videos were near their 2023 peak during the Robotyne fighting: 135 in July and 126 in August.
A Lancet-3 was filmed striking an abandoned Leopard 2A6 after 8 June 2023.
A Lancet hit an 82nd Air Assault Brigade Stryker east of Robotyne on 15 August 2023.
Russian sources claimed that EW "severely interfered" with Ukrainian GPS devices and drone controls on 8 June 2023 (reported by ISW).
Russian trench jammers along the Robotyne belt reportedly brought Ukrainian drones down "in scores" in 2023.
Ukrainian night-bomber drones in the 2023 Zaporizhzhia offensive were committed only when Russian EW relaxed (RUSI).
Only 3% of Ukrainian fire missions in the 2023 offensive were smoke, because smoke blinded the drone feeds that headquarters used to run the fight (RUSI).

observations.subject: share of Ukrainian fire missions that were smoke

text: Russian Ka-52 strikes in summer 2023 came from 8–10 km and were "often heralded by the lifting of GPS jamming among Russian formations", because both armies use many of the same navigation-dependent platforms (RUSI).

cites.quote: often heralded by the lifting of GPS jamming among Russian formations

text: Russian helicopter groups often flew with an EW escort carrying directional pods aimed at radar in summer 2023 (RUSI).
RUSI reports two more Russian signatures: frequencies reset every 24 hours, and electronic protection dipped when precise coordinates were needed.
notes: The file adds that no source found reports a GPS-jamming tell before Lancet launches or artillery.

text: By September–October 2023 Russia had the FPV edge in the 47th Mechanised Brigade's sector, and Russian FPVs hunted equipment and dugouts around Robotyne.
At the end of November 2023 Russian milbloggers said the weather was hampering vehicles and artillery but not drones.
Ukrainian drone operators said Russia "significantly increased electronic warfare (EW) jamming since fall 2023".

cites.quote: significantly increased electronic warfare (EW) jamming since fall 2023

text: In early 2024 about 100 drones of both sides could operate at once within a 10 km radius (via ISW).

observations.subject: drones of both sides operating at once within a 10 km radius

text: In early 2024 one Ukrainian brigade detected 70–90 Russian FPVs a day (via ISW).

observations.subject: Russian FPVs detected by one brigade

text: Russian FPV control bands spread from 850–930 MHz to 720–1020 MHz in 2024.
notes: The bullet cites both sources jointly for the bands and the jammer modules.

text: Ukrainian vehicle jammers went from one module to seven within 2024 as Russian FPV bands spread.

observations.subject: Ukrainian vehicle jammer, by end of 2024

notes: The bullet cites both sources jointly.

text: Russian vehicles gained Volnorez jammer domes in autumn 2023.
Russian vehicles gained "turtle" jammer boxes in April 2024.
Dedicated video jamming of drones appeared in summer 2024, and dedicated video-jamming platforms in the second half of 2024.
Russian Orlan and Zala orbits reached 1,000–1,500 a day by August 2024 (RUSI).
In 2024 60–80% of Ukrainian FPVs failed to reach their targets (RUSI).
Russia fielded fibre-optic FPVs, immune to jamming, from August 2024 in Kursk Oblast.
A Ukrainian EW commander dates the "collapse" of conventional front-line jamming to the end of 2024.
Rubikon, founded in August 2024, put over 25% of its strikes on Ukrainian drone teams by September 2025.

observations.subject: share of Rubikon strikes on Ukrainian drone teams

text: The drone kill zone deepened to 10–15 km by 2025.
Ukraine answered Russian jamming with terminal autonomy for the last ~500 m of a drone's flight (2025).
Ukraine fielded interceptor drones against Russian reconnaissance UAVs (2025).
Lancet strike videos fell after August 2023, to 59 in December 2023.
The Ukrainian Air Force counted 10,604 Lancets destroyed by August 2026.

effect: defeats the night-bombing tactic while active; effects dramatic when it relaxes
rationale: RUSI: in June 2023 the bombers were 'binary' in viability; with Russian EW active they could not get in and usually were not committed.

effect: shoots down Orlan-10s
rationale: Ukrainian units downed Orlan-10s with MANPADS, ten reported on 1 May 2022 alone.

effect: combined countermeasure against Orlan-10
rationale: The 2023 answer to the Orlan-10 was 'a combination of countermeasures involving electronic warfare stations and firepower'.

effect: jams the Orlan-10
rationale: Bukovel-AD has been in service against the Orlan-10 since 2016.

counter: detecting and jamming the Orlan-10 master aircraft's 930 MHz link
effect: killing the master aircraft takes the whole group out (analyst argument)
rationale: Armada argued the master link could be passively detected and jammed and that killing one aircraft takes the three-ship group out.

counter: Ukrainian EW station against spotter drones
measure: Zala and Orlan spotting for Lancet
effect: aims to blind the spotters so they cannot adjust Lancets (stated aim)
rationale: A late-2023 Ukrainian EW station was announced to 'blind Zala and Orlan so that they can no longer adjust their Lancets to our positions'.

effect: thins Russian Orlans and Zalas
rationale: RUSI: radar-cued interceptor drones began thinning Orlans and Zalas only from late 2024; KSE reports interceptor drones against Russian reconnaissance UAVs in 2025.

effect: several net layers protect against it
rationale: Kyiv Post: camouflage netting on a metal frame was the most effective defence; several net layers protect against the Lancet-1; two Lancets failed against a T-72 because a net stopped them.

effect: degrades: a net-triggered warhead is unlikely to cause significant damage compared to a direct hit
rationale: Kyiv Independent: a net-triggered Lancet warhead 'is unlikely to cause significant damage compared to a direct hit'; both sides netted guns and equipment in 2023.

effect: partly defeats nets: the warhead can be set off after the net is hit
rationale: Kyiv Post: the Lancet-3 is harder to stop because its warhead can be set off remotely after it hits the net.

effect: defeats nets and cages
rationale: By November 2023 a newer Lancet pre-detonated its shaped charge to defeat nets and cages.

counter: Ukrainian drone strikes on EW emitters
effect: forces dispersal: Zhitel used more subtly, antennas dismounted, Pole-21 treated as disposable
rationale: RUSI: in summer 2023 Russia moved away from large single platforms because Ukraine targeted emitters; a growing number of Pole-21 kills was reported and one was destroyed in the Tavria sector in November 2023.

effect: cuts drones off from their operators so they fall 'in scores' (soldier's claim)
rationale: Suitcase-size trench jamming stations around Robotyne in summer–autumn 2023 reportedly brought Ukrainian drones down 'in scores'.

effect: puts a jamming dome over the vehicle
rationale: The Volnorez vehicle cone jammer put a 'dome' over a vehicle against FPVs from autumn 2023.

counter: Russian jamming of DJI control and video links
effect: drone descends or is forced to land, often unrecoverable
rationale: IEEE: OcuSync 'was not built for dense jamming' and a jammer attacking both signals often leaves the drone unrecoverable; operators near Bakhmut and in the south reported drones descending or forced to land in March 2023.

effect: takes control of drones and geolocates operators
rationale: Shipovnik-Aero takes over drones and geolocates operators for artillery; Ukrainian sources rated it 'particularly effective'.

effect: cut its hit rate from 55% to 6%
rationale: Ukrainian data relayed by Kyiv Post: Excalibur's hit rate fell from 55% in January 2023 to 6% in August 2023.

effect: contributes to Ukrainian drone losses of about 10,000 a month
rationale: RUSI: Russia's extensive navigational interference contributed to Ukrainian drone losses of about 10,000 a month in spring 2023; drones that lose link and orientation crash or drift.

counter: Russian platoon jammers and UAV-hijacking arrays
effect: directional jamming of drone links and drone takeover
rationale: RUSI: at least one counter-UAS system per platoon in Russian line infantry by spring 2023.

counter: switching to a frequency the Russians cannot easily exploit
effect: picture returns within seconds
rationale: AP: an Asgard Group pilot switched frequency when jammed and the picture returned within seconds; the unit took three months to learn to evade the jammers.

measure: Russian jamming of 5.8 GHz FPV video
effect: less jammed and penetrates obstacles better
rationale: IEEE: FPV video moved from 5.8 GHz towards 1.2 GHz, which was less jammed (by early 2024).

counter: higher-power video transmitters and two-way repeaters
effect: more than doubles practical range
rationale: IEEE: builders gained video transmitters of up to 5 W and volunteer repeaters that 'more than double the practical range'.

effect: closes the backdoors that let drones be tracked
rationale: Volunteers patched DJI firmware and 'closed the backdoors that allowed the drones to be tracked by Aeroscope'; units disabled or patched out Remote ID.

counter: terrain-shielded pre-programmed flight and emission-silent missions
effect: crews live longer, at the cost of slower targeting
rationale: RUSI 2022: crews who pre-programmed paths shielded by terrain lived longer; some flew without transmitting and downloaded images on recovery.

effect: switches Remote ID off without overwriting firmware
rationale: In early May 2022 Ukrainian operators obtained a program that switches Remote ID off.

counter: DJI firmware with Remote ID locked on
effect: makes some older models detectable again
rationale: About June 2022 DJI shipped firmware in which Remote ID can no longer be switched off.

effect: evades the DJI sensor
rationale: Aerorozvidka built its own R18 partly to evade the DJI sensor; units moved to non-DJI drones.

effect: locates the pilot; targeting can begin in about 5–6 minutes
rationale: A Ukrainian unit said Russia could begin targeting operators via AeroScope in as little as five or six minutes; DroneID broadcast the pilot's position unencrypted; Aerorozvidka cited Ukrainians killed by AeroScope users.

effect: fires follow in about 20–30 minutes
rationale: Shipovnik-Aero geolocated operators for artillery in spring 2023; RUSI gives about 20–30 minutes for fires cued by EW detection.

effect: intercepts and decrypts in near real time
rationale: RUSI: Torn-MDM intercepted and decrypted Ukrainian Motorola radios in near real time, front-wide.

measure: RF jamming of drone control links
effect: immune to jamming
rationale: Russia fielded fibre-optic FPVs, immune to jamming, from August 2024 in Kursk.

measure: RF jamming of drone control links
effect: terminal autonomy for the last ~500 m
rationale: Ukraine answered with terminal autonomy for the last ~500 m.

effect: blinds the drone feeds (including one's own)
rationale: RUSI: only 3% of Ukrainian fire missions were smoke because smoke blinded the drone feeds headquarters used.

counter: close-range drone use near own antennas
effect: drones closer to their control antennae than to enemy jammers stay usable
rationale: RUSI found drones more useful in defence partly because in the close they are nearer their control antennae than enemy jamming.
